verdicts.why: Describes the light, bright quality of the gay feeling the gloss names, contrasts it with a neighbour, stays inside the word; positive charge fits.
Same joy-and-pleasure sense as the gloss, distinguished from gladness only by fuller form and a formal register label; positive charge fits.
Joy and pleasure actively felt matches the gloss, and the placement between contentment and merriment is a word-internal comparison; positive charge fits.
Literary is an allowed register label and the note keeps the gloss's joy-and-pleasure sense, differing from gladness only in ornament; positive charge fits.
Bare commendation of soundness matches the gloss exactly, the example fits this sense, and the positive charge is right.
Plain word for feeling grief, neither approving nor blaming, matches the gloss and the neutral charge.
Keeps to the gloss's practical soundness rather than drifting to the initiative sense, informal is a register label, and positive fits.
Plain term for the feeling of well-being matches the gloss, stays inside the word, positive charge fits.
Slang register and the cool, job-done framing of a premeditated killing describe this gloss's sense against murder; negative charge fits.
Informal and blunt naming of sound practical judgment matches the gloss, compared within the family; positive charge fits.
The note calls the word a 'neutral faculty-name' while the entry's charge is positive, so the note and the charge contradict each other on the one thing the charge is meant to record.

Names the ability to tell relations apart as the plain member of a family whose loaded member is sagacity; that is a within-family intensity contrast, and positive remains plausible for an ability-gloss.
Formal praise for judgment that turns out well matches the 'good judgment' gloss and distinguishes it from the bare faculty; positive charge fits.
